speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your symptoms, could you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, such as whether it consists of spots, blisters, or raised bumps?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression from a facial rash to the trunk and extremities, along with the prodromal symptoms, is highly characteristic. Are the lesions on her face described as having a "slapped cheek" appearance, and are the body lesions lacy or reticular in pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic progression of symptoms, including the facial rash sparing the perioral area and the subsequent lacy body rash, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
